4.t: EDITORIAL
When school opened in September it was found that a new Principal had been
appointed- Fr. Cyril Barrett, S.J. He was not new to Wah Yan as the had been
Rector and Principal from 1956 until 1962, and had already spent last year （1969-70）
on the teaching staff. Fr. Deignan had left Wah Yan and gone to Ricci Hall as War-
den where some of our Senior Students hope to meet him again. We wish him
every success and happiness in his new field of work.
Mrs. Agnes Ng retired from teaching having been on the Wah Yan staff since
1932 with the exception of the war years. Mr. K.M. Chan, and Miss May Miok Join-
ed the Staff in September '70. Brother L. Thoo, S.J. left for the U.S.A. in January
and Mr. Gary Lam S.J. joined the Staff. In Aoril Miss Y.Y. Tam left and went
abroad.
December 4th was the day of the Pope's flying visit to Hong Kong and it was
a great thrill for us in Wah Yan, as well as for a great number of Hong Kong folk.
Several hundred of our boys were at the Stadium. We too felt the tension as the
clatter of the helicopter made itself felt coming towards the Valley. Then the man，
Paul, himself! To see him and to hear his voice - his slow, measured tones 一
this was a memory to treasure.
The Students Council continues its work in the school. It has altogether 31
ciubs and societies affiliated to it. Beginning with the Altar Soclety the list goes
on to the Bowling Club, Bridge Club, Boxing Club. The list is too long to give in
full, but readers will find in the pages of the Star a report from each society. Each
Club and each form from Form 2 to Form Upper Six inclusive sends representatives
to its meetings: There are 54 Councillors in all. The Council appointed Committee
to organize our School Drama Festival and will organize and host this year's Secon-
Our Social Activities Club helped run a week long summer camp for 200 poor
Children of Western District; during Xmas vacation a Games' Day was conducted in
Ming Lun Primary School in Taipo with the welccme help of the Social Service Group
of St. Francis Canossian College; and during Chinese New Year holidays the club
held a Fair for poor children of Wanchai with the helo of the Ying Wa Girls.
Our own School Athletic meet in October '70 revealed more talent than we
had dared to hope for. New records were made in the A grade Shot Put, the C
grade 80m. Low Hurdles, the C grade High Jump and the C grade Shot Put. The
increase in the number of participants in C and D grades gives grounds for hope
of greater athletic success in future. We entered a small team - 15 only - in the
Inter-School Athletic meet at the end of March '71. We gained 2 firsts and enough
places to make us look forward with confidence to the next meet. Our B grade
Badminton won the Championship Cup While our C grade ー a completely new team
- got 3rd place.

5.t: Many of our pupils now look for a short road to health and strength in Judo
and Chinese Boxing. These two sports are, maybe, a response to the violence of
the concrete jungle we live in.
Within the space of 3 months, the deaths were announced of 3 Jesuits who
were at one period very much a part of the college- Fr: Sheridan who died in
Manila had taught as a Scholastic in Robinson Road '34-'36 and who had come
back after the war to teach again, to write or revise our history text-books and above
all to found the Wah Yan Past Students Dramatic Society. Fr. Ryan had been on
the teaching Staff from 1934 until 1938. He had indeed never been out.of touch
with Wah Yan Students even during the war years in Kweilin and Chungking. He
had two periods of teaching in the post war years and had spent his years of re-
tirement in the College before he died at the age of 81. Fr. Maguire was best known
as Sportsmaster and as Headmaster of the P.M. School 1949 - 1952. Fr. Rory's
death came as a very painful shock as he was killed in a road accident in his na-
tive Ireland. May they rest in peace！
Our Wah Yan Past Students Dramatic Society is now in the 24th year of its
life. Fr. Sheridan had written the play for the March 1971 performance at the City
Hall and was to have come from Manila to see it througn its final rehearsals when
death intervened. Nothing daunted, in the true spirit of their founder, the Dramatic
Society put on their play and played to capacity houses in the City Hall for four nights.
Our examination results were good without being remarkable. Three Form 5
e Matriculation Course. In the Matricula-students were awarded Scholarships to th
ticn examination 47 out of 56 matriculated; 27 were admitted to the University of
Hong Kong and a further 8 gained places in universities abroad.
Fr. Pedro Arrupe, Superior General of the Society of Jesus paid a two day
visit to Hong Kong. He met all the Hong Kong and Macau Jesuits on Monday 19th
at our school, addressed them and concelebrated Mass with them.He met also a
great number of people who are involved with the Fathers in this work, teachers，
schoolboys and above all the relatives of the members of the Society who were in
Hong Kong. Of those who met Fr. Arrupe on that occasion not many will forget the
man, small in physical size but immensely big in the warmth and vitality of his per-
sonality.
The Night School still continues. There is less demand for places in the lower
Classes put the ton forms continue to be as full as ever. An old boys' society has
just been startea.
At the end of April, agreement was reached with the Pun U Association that
Wah Yan take over their Primary School, which is situated at Shiu Fai Terrace. The
supervisor will be our Principal, Fr. Barrett and the Headmaster Fr. Joseph Mallin，
S.J. The school Will be known as the Pun U Association Wah Yan Primary School.
The Past Students Association has remained very active. Its aim is to keep
in touch with the past of all the years of the college and to keep the past in touch
with the college. Our Senior students are very grateful for the very useful Careers
Taiks organised by the Past.

As quite a number of enquiries have
recently been made, especially by past stu-
dents, as to how contributions may be made
to the Scholarship Fund, it seems best to
gIve a brief outline of the scheme for those
interested.
The fund was set up to help students
of intellectual promise who might be handr-
capped in their studies by. financial prob-
lems.In the annual reward or renewal of
the scholarships both the progress and the
financial status of the students are taken
Over the years since the fund was set
up the number of scholarship has grown so
that now there are some 50 available each
year. 1hese scholarships are Of three Kinds.
First, there is the “founded' or perpetual
scholarship where the donor gives a capital
sum of $5000 which yielas an annual sum
The donors arrange to
have the scholarship nameo, often to com-
nemorate some relative or friend. Secondly，
there are benefactors who commit them-
selves to donate each vear one or more
scholarships of $300 or $400. Finally, from
time to time, donors come forward with a
scholarship for one year_without any com-
mitment to renew it.
This latter type is
usually awarded to students in their final
year of studies.
As those students awarded scholarships
also qualify for a remission of tuition fees，
they usually have enough in hand to cover
all other school expenses such as travel，
books and equipment.
In this connection，
because of casual donations made to the
sChool from time to time and added to the
fund, the school is also able to help other
students with the purchase of books and
uniforms where the need exists.
Among the donors are prominent per-
sons in Hong Kong, fathers of students and
quite a number of past students.
Several
scholarships have been donated by groups
of past students who have long left the
school.
The recent past, too, have played
their part. Some have sent donations from
abroad and more than one who was himself
helped through his studies by a scholarship
has donated one to the school as a mark
of gratitude.
At present, a group of stu-
dents, many of them still in the school, are
getting together to raise funds for yet an-
other scholarship.
It has always been the aim
of Wah
Yan College that every student of ability，
whatever his financial status, should have
equal opportunity to be successful in his
studies.
This Scholarship Fund as it grows
from year to vear will go far to help main-
tain this aim.
The school is deeply grateful
to those who have made this fund available.
